text:
Carolina arrives with its form intact: a 9-2 win over Chicago five days ago, 4-1-0 in its last five, and outscoring opponents 25-11 in that stretch. The Hurricanes are without Jordan Staal (calf), and Jackson Blake has taken his spot beside Martinook and Ehlers. Seattle comes in 2-3-0 after a 4-3 home loss to the Rangers, missing Jared McCann, Curtis Douglas and Jacob Melanson, with Matty Beniers on the first power-play unit and Shane Wright up to 16:31 a night.

The gap in chance quality is wide. Carolina has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of shots taken and allowed) at five on five, Seattle 45%, and our model projects 3.58 goals to 2.52. Carolina's power play creates 0.9 expected goals a game against Seattle's 0.58. In net, projected starter Pyotr Kochetkov is 9.8 goals saved above expected this season, while Philipp Grubauer sits at -0.8 after a .866 stretch over his last five starts. Grubauer was 5.35 above expected last season, but Kochetkov was roughly even.

Blake has a nine-game point streak, and we have him at 62% for a point. Logan Stankoven, drafted 47th overall in 2021, is at 54% for a point. Sebastian Aho leads the Hurricanes at 35% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Mark Jankowski: his shots have produced 4.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, and we have him at 23% to score. For Seattle, watch Berkly Catton, the eighth pick in 2024, on an eight-game point streak.
